plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Pale lilac-pink goblets rise straight from bare ground, with no leaves in sight. They carpet damp meadows and light woodland edges like a soft purple mist just as autumn deepens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (roughly September to October)
plants.location: Meadows and woodlands across Western and Central Europe, including the UK, France and Germany
plants.funFact: The flowers appear in autumn, but the leaves and seed capsules show up the following spring. This odd timing earned it the nickname 'naked ladies'. Every part of the plant contains colchicine, a potent toxin that is also used in plant breeding and medicine.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets turn violet-blue as this graceful tree erupts in clouds of trumpet-shaped blossoms. Fallen petals pile up beneath it like a lavender carpet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November, peaking mid-October to early November)
plants.location: Pretoria and Johannesburg in South Africa, plus Sydney, Australia and Buenos Aires, Argentina
plants.funFact: Native to South America, the jacaranda is now so tied to the October bloom in Pretoria, nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City', that local lore says a petal landing on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: Airy, feathery foliage carries daisy-like flowers that sway on slender stems. Their bright petals surround golden centers and draw swarms of bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer through the first frost (often into mid-October in temperate regions)
plants.location: Gardens and roadsides across the temperate Northern Hemisphere, including the United States and Europe, with wild roots in Mexico
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Greek word 'kosmos', meaning order or harmony, a nod to the neat symmetry of the petals. Regular deadheading can keep the plant flowering until a hard frost ends the season.
